/**
 * repair/adapters.ts — HTTP adapters (fetch wrappers) for the repair
 * deep module.
 *
 * Foundation slice (issue #285): this file is intentionally empty. The
 * adapter functions currently live in `../api.ts`; they will be migrated
 * here by later slices of PRD #284. The empty placeholder establishes
 * the file path and the public surface for the deep module without
 * changing runtime behavior.
 *
 * Once the migration lands, this module will own the canonical URLs and
 * the `fetch` wrappers for:
 *   - createRepair, getRepair, transitionRepairStatus, updateRepairNotes
 *   - getCustomerWithBicycles, startWorkTimer, stopWorkTimer
 *   - getRepairs (paginated list), completeRepairPayment
 *   - getRepairsForWeek (calendar view)
 *   - fetchWorkers, searchParts, fetchLaborServices (new in PRD #284)
 *
 * Until then, callers should continue to import adapter functions from
 * `../api.js`.
 */

// Placeholder export so this file is a module (cannot `export {}` from an
// otherwise-empty file without making the barrel's `export *` include
// nothing meaningful). The export name documents the slice's intent.
export const __adapters_pending_migration = true

/**
 * repair/index.ts — Public face of the repair deep module.
 *
 * This barrel is the single import path for the rest of the
 * `client/src/features/repairs/` feature. Anything NOT re-exported here
 * is module-internal and must not be reached from outside this folder.
 *
 * The folder structure is:
 *
 *   repair/
 *   ├── index.ts       ← public barrel (this file)
 *   ├── types.ts       ← canonical type re-exports
 *   ├── adapters.ts    ← HTTP fetch wrappers
 *   ├── formatters.ts  ← pure format helpers
 *   └── domain.ts      ← status machine + VAT rate constants
 *
 * Foundation slice (issue #285): the barrel exposes the canonical types
 * and the placeholder sub-modules. Later slices of PRD #284 will
 * populate `adapters.ts`, `formatters.ts`, and `domain.ts` and extend
 * the barrel with hooks (`useRepairList`, `useRepairDetail`,
 * `useRepairCalendar`) and helper functions.
 *
 * ─── Architect sign-off required ───
 *
 * The barrel's public surface is the contract that every later slice
 * builds on. Changes to the names exported here ripple through every
 * consumer. Per issue #285's acceptance criteria, the `architect` skill
 * must sign off on this surface before subsequent slices land.
 *
 * Affected concepts:
 *   - Canonical repair types (statuses, hold reasons, intake input,
 *     detail shape, line items, work logs, status history)
 *   - Public surface of the deep module's three sub-modules
 *
 * Structural decision:
 *   - The deep module's name is `repair/` (not `repair-client/` or
 *     `repair.service.ts`) — matches ADR-008 (Flow-First Architecture).
 *   - `types.ts` re-exports from `@shared/types/repair`; the shared
 *     module remains the single source of truth for these shapes.
 *   - Client-only shapes (e.g. `PaginatedRepairs.breakdown`) will be
 *     added to `types.ts` in later slices, not to `shared/`.
 *
 * Boundary implications:
 *   - The `../api.ts` re-export layer remains in this foundation slice
 *     so that existing call sites (`import { createRepair } from
 *     '../api.js'`) keep working without modification. Later slices
 *     will move adapter functions from `api.ts` into
 *     `repair/adapters.ts` and reduce `api.ts` to a thin re-export
 *     from this deep module.
 *   - The existing client-local `../types.ts` (with `STATUS_COLORS` and
 *     the `RepairDetailWithCustomer` view-shape) stays at its current
 *     path for this slice. A later slice will decide whether
 *     `STATUS_COLORS` belongs in `repair/formatters.ts` (it is a
 *     presentation concern, not a domain type) or stays where it is.
 *
 * Source-of-truth impact: none in this slice. The shared module remains
 * canonical for all types re-exported here.
 *
 * Allowed implementation direction: import from this barrel anywhere
 * inside `client/src/features/repairs/`. Do NOT import from this
 * barrel from outside the feature.
 *
 * Forbidden shortcuts:
 *   - Do not add new `as` type assertions in production code (CONTEXT.md).
 *   - Do not import from the deep module's sub-files directly; use
 *     this barrel so the public surface is the only path in.
 *   - Do not move types out of `shared/` into this module — shared
 *     remains the source of truth.
 */

// ─── Types — canonical, re-exported from shared ──────────────────────
//
// The foundation slice exposes the minimum type surface required by the
// issue's acceptance criteria. Later slices will extend this list as
// they add adapters, formatters, hooks, and client-only shapes
// (e.g. `PaginatedRepairs.breakdown`).
export type {
  RepairStatus,
  Repair,
  RepairDetail,
  RepairLineItem,
  WorkLog,
  RepairIntakeInput,
  LaborService,
  HoldReason,
} from './types.js'
export { VALID_TRANSITIONS } from './types.js'

// ─── Sub-modules — placeholder until later slices populate them ───────
//
// Each sub-module currently exposes a single placeholder constant. The
// `export *` form keeps the barrel forward-compatible: when a later
// slice adds real exports to the sub-modules, they flow through this
// barrel automatically without a barrel change.
export * as adapters from './adapters.js'
export * as formatters from './formatters.js'
export * as domain from './domain.js'

/**
 * repair/types.ts — Public type surface of the repair deep module.
 *
 * Re-exports the canonical repair types from `@shared/types/repair`. The
 * shared module is the single source of truth for these shapes — the
 * client feature MUST NOT re-declare them. Any client-only additions
 * (e.g. `PaginatedRepairs` with the `breakdown` field) live here, not in
 * `shared/`.
 *
 * Foundation slice (issue #285): this file is a thin re-export of the
 * canonical types listed in the issue's acceptance criteria:
 *   `RepairStatus`, `Repair`, `RepairDetail`, `RepairLineItem`,
 *   `WorkLog`, `RepairIntakeInput`, `LaborService`, `HoldReason`,
 *   `VALID_TRANSITIONS`.
 *
 * Sub-files of the deep module (`adapters.ts`, `formatters.ts`,
 * `domain.ts`) are placeholders; they will be filled by later slices.
 * Additional types from `@shared/types/repair` may be re-exported here
 * in those later slices — the foundation slice keeps the surface to the
 * minimum required by the issue's AC so the architect can sign off on
 * a focused public contract.
 */

export type {
  RepairStatus,
  Repair,
  RepairDetail,
  RepairLineItem,
  WorkLog,
  RepairIntakeInput,
  LaborService,
  HoldReason,
} from '@shared/types/repair.js'

export { VALID_TRANSITIONS } from '@shared/types/repair.js'

/**
 * repair/domain.ts — Domain constants and rules for the repair deep
 * module.
 *
 * Foundation slice (issue #285): this file is intentionally empty. The
 * status-machine and VAT-rate knowledge (`VALID_TRANSITIONS` is
 * re-exported from `types.ts`) are currently scattered across
 * `api.ts` (ACTIVE_STATUSES), `RepairDetailPage.tsx` (vatRateMap), and
 * inline in components. They will be consolidated here by later slices
 * of PRD #284.
 *
 * Once the migration lands, this module will own:
 *   - ACTIVE_STATUSES, TERMINAL_STATUSES
 *   - isActiveStatus, isTerminalStatus
 *   - VAT_RATE_IDS, vatRateIdForBps
 *   - getWorkerName (if it stays as a one-liner; otherwise left in
 *     components)
 *
 * Until then, callers should continue to use the inline constants in
 * their current locations.
 */

// Placeholder export so this file is a module.
export const __domain_pending_migration = true

/**
 * repair/formatters.ts — Pure formatting helpers for the repair deep

 *
 * Foundation slice (issue #285): this file is intentionally empty. The

# ADR-008: Flow-First Architecture — Consolidate Transaction Logic

**Status**: ✅ Accepted  
**Date**: 2026-05-21  
**Authors**: David De Block  

---

## Context

The codebase was structured around "features" using `todos` as a demo template (ADR-001). Each feature is self-contained with its own components, hooks, services, and routes in `features/[name]/` folders.

This works well for independent CRUD modules (products, customers) but **breaks down for the primary business flow** — the sale transaction. A sale touches products, stock, sequences, payments, and documents simultaneously. With feature-per-domain, this atomic operation is scattered across 5+ directories (`sales`, `stock-validator`, `sequences`), forcing callers to manage cross-imports and coordinate state between features.

The complexity of coordinating a transaction leaks into every boundary instead of living in one place. This makes the sale flow hard to test, hard to understand, and hard to modify safely.

---

## Decision Drivers

---
ADR-006-golden-copy-pattern.md
ADR-007-sequence-table-for-document-numbering.md
ADR-008-flow-first-architecture.md
ADR-009-issue-interaction-contract.md
ADR-010-e2e-test-strategy.md

# Handoff: Repair Frontend Deep Module

> **Source:** `improve-codebase-architecture` analysis of `client/src/features/repairs/` (2026-06-05).
> **Origin:** User asked to look at the repairs feature for deepening opportunities; this handoff packages candidates 1 and 2 of that analysis.

## Context

The backend `server/src/services/repair.service.ts` is genuinely deep — it owns the atomic complete-repair transaction, the status state machine, hold-reason validation, and the cross-entity orchestration. ADR-008 (flow-first) was applied to the server.

The **client-side repairs feature has no equivalent module.** Component total: 5,158 lines. Types: 110 lines. Domain logic in the client: ~0. Every screen re-declares the types it needs, re-fetches what it needs, re-formats what it needs, and re-implements the same state machines.

The most visible symptom: `client/src/features/repairs/components/RepairDetailPage.tsx` is **2,078 lines** with **20+ useState** and **7 useEffect**, holding 7+ orthogonal concerns (timer, notes, dates, line items, worker assignment, status transition, payment, special items) in a single component.

A real bug has already shipped because of the shallow architecture: the four KPI cards on the list page ("Active / In progress / Ready for pickup / Overdue") iterate over the **current page's** `repairs` array instead of the full dataset, so "Active: 7" actually means "active on this page". The team has not noticed because no test exercises the KPI block.

## Architectural decisions agreed with the user

1. **Deep module shape — Per-entity hooks (Shape C).** The new `client/src/features/repairs/repair/` folder exposes three per-entity hooks (`useRepairList`, `useRepairDetail`, `useRepairCalendar`) plus shared adapters, formatters, and domain constants. Each hook owns its own state.
2. **Page split pattern — Focused interaction hooks (Pattern Y) + section components in separate files.** The detail page becomes a pure orchestrator that composes focused hooks and renders section components.
3. **High-leverage hooks in scope:** `useRepairTimer`, `useRepairNotes`, `useRepairLineItems`. Other concerns (dates, worker assignment, status transition, special item workflow) are follow-up PRDs.
4. **`SpecialItemForm` is owned by `useRepairLineItems`.** The two-step workflow (create part → add as line item) lives in the hook; the form is a presentational child.
5. **Section components in separate files** (`TimerSection.tsx`, `NotesSection.tsx`, `LineItemsSection.tsx`) in `components/`.
6. **KPI bug fix in scope (small).** Fix by adding a `breakdown` field to the paginated response — server computes counts-by-status alongside the row query, hook reads it, page renders from it.
7. **Cache sharing — module-level Map for `useRepairDetail`.** When the list page's row expand warms the cache, the detail page's mount hits warm. No global store, no React context — plain `Map<id, { data, fetchedAt }>` in the hook module. TTL: none (matches current behavior).
8. **Deep module file structure — folder `repair/` with `index.ts` (barrel) + 4 sub-files** (`types.ts`, `adapters.ts`, `formatters.ts`, `domain.ts`).
9. **One PRD, three PRs.** Each PR is independently shippable; each has its own review surface.

## Duplication catalog (the deletion-test failures being fixed)

| Duplicated thing | Current callsites | New home |
|---|---|---|
| Enriched `RepairDetail` shape | `api.ts`, `RepairDetailPage.tsx`, `RepairRowExpandPanel.tsx` (param) | `repair/types.ts` (re-export) |
| `formatStatus` helper | `RepairCard.tsx`, `RepairListPage.tsx`, `RepairRowExpandPanel.tsx` | `repair/formatters.ts` |
| `getWorkerName` helper | `RepairCard.tsx`, `RepairListPage.tsx`, `RepairRowExpandPanel.tsx` | `repair/domain.ts` (or stay in component if just a one-liner) |
| `epochToInputDate` / `inputDateToEpoch` | `RepairDetailPage.tsx`, `ReschedulePopover.tsx` | `repair/formatters.ts` |
| `WorkerOption` interface | `RepairCard.tsx`, `RepairListPage.tsx`, `RepairDetailPage.tsx` | `repair/types.ts` (re-exported from `shared/types/staff.ts` if it fits) |
| `fetch('/api/users')` | `RepairListPage.tsx`, `RepairCalendarView.tsx`, `RepairDetailPage.tsx` | `repair/adapters.ts` as `fetchWorkers()` |
| `VALID_TRANSITIONS` map | `shared/types/repair.ts` (canonical) + `RepairDetailPage.tsx` (re-declared) | `repair/domain.ts` re-exports the canonical one |
| `fetch('/api/parts')` (parts search) | `RepairDetailPage.tsx` | `repair/adapters.ts` as `searchParts(query)` |
| `fetch('/api/repairs/labor-services')` | `RepairDetailPage.tsx` | `repair/adapters.ts` as `fetchLaborServices()` |
| VAT rate ID mapping (2100/600/0 → vat-standard/vat-reduced/vat-zero) | `RepairDetailPage.tsx` (inline `vatRateMap`) | `repair/domain.ts` |
| `paginated list + page iteration` KPI computation | `RepairListPage.tsx` (incorrect) | `useRepairList` returns `breakdown` from server |

## Test survival matrix

| Layer | Test fate |
|---|---|
| `api.test.ts` | Evolves into `repair/__tests__/adapters.test.ts` |
| `useRepairDetailCache.test.ts` | Becomes `hooks/__tests__/useRepairDetail.test.ts` |
| `useRepairsForWeek.test.ts` | Becomes `hooks/__tests__/useRepairCalendar.test.ts` |
| `dateAnchor.test.ts` | Becomes `repair/__tests__/domain.test.ts` |
| `RepairCard.test.tsx`, `RepairIntakeModal.test.tsx`, `RepairRowExpandPanel.test.tsx`, `ReschedulePopover.test.tsx`, `RepairCalendarView.test.tsx` | **Unchanged** — none touch the god page |
| New: `useRepairList`, `useRepairTimer`, `useRepairNotes`, `useRepairLineItems` | New focused test files |
| New: section components | New focused test files |
| New: `repair/formatters`, `repair/domain` | New unit test files |

No existing test file is deleted in this PRD; one (`useRepairDetailCache`) is renamed + extended; the rest either stay or evolve.

## Migration order (3 PRs)

1. **PR 1 — Deep module + per-entity data hooks + KPI fix.** Net effect: data layer consolidated, bug fixed.
2. **PR 2 — Detail page part 1: `useRepairTimer` + `TimerSection`, `useRepairNotes` + `NotesSection`.** Net effect: page shrinks from 2,078 → ~1,400 lines.
3. **PR 3 — Detail page part 2: `useRepairLineItems` + `LineItemsSection` + `SpecialItemForm` extraction.** Net effect: page lands at ~250 lines.

## Out of scope for this PRD (follow-ups)

- `useRepairDates`, `useRepairWorkerAssignment`, `useRepairStatusTransition` — same pattern as the three in-scope hooks, smaller scope.
- The custom combobox extraction (`useCombobox` + `<Combobox>` in `client/src/shared/ui/`) — natural follow-up after this PRD lands; ~4 callers would benefit.
- Adopting TanStack Query / SWR — a separate ADR; the module-level Map is the right size for now.
- Other candidates from the `improve-codebase-architecture` analysis (KPI bug — fixed in PR 1; SpecialItemForm — fixed in PR 3; combobox pattern — out of scope).
